answers.answer: Roll one die simultaneously for each held office card. Add one for each fatigue on that card, and the Chairman adds one more. On modified 1–2, nothing happens; 3–4 adds fatigue; 5+ retires the officeholder. Move the retiring member to Pensioners, flip the office card into Vacant Offices, and return that card's fatigue to the supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make these normal office attrition rolls.
answers.evidence: London Season—Attrition: ‘Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire.’

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner may take or discard a London Season display card. They act in descending order of their actual total retirement spending; ties go first to the player with the most total windows, counting new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. Do not replace a selected or discarded card while selection is underway. If the display empties, skip every remaining eligible player immediately. At the end, discard every remaining display card and refill exactly three cards—prestige faceup and blackmail facedown—even if nobody selected a card. Return all unused Pensioners to their supplies.
answers.evidence: London Season—Prestige: eligible retirees, spending/window/PM order, empty-display rule, refill, and Pensioner return.

answers.answer: At the start of your Family phase action, check whether the opportunity marker already matches the main action you choose. You may take that main action twice if it matched at phase start; otherwise take it once. Then move the marker onto the chosen action. Afterward, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action; the marker never doubles that extra action and is not moved by it. With four vacant offices and the marker already on Enlist Writer, take Enlist Writer twice, placing two writers, and the four-vacancy bonus adds one writer once this turn: three writers total.
answers.evidence: Family: marker checked at phase start; Writer with at least four vacant offices adds one writer once this turn.

answers.answer: After all players finish Family actions, if both Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant from the Stock Exchange into Court as a Company share and lower Debt by one. Repeat while both Debt and applicants remain. If Debt is zero, slide all remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. Seeking a share pays the printed queue-space cost to the bank; it does not pay family cash into Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Family—New Company shares: rightmost applicant enters Court while Debt remains; no-Debt applicants slide right; Seek Share pays bank.

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending number shown on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that member into the office; the member's owner receives the office card. Hiring your own family in the ordinary way requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool. When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and put the old card, now vacant, into ascending hiring order. If there is no candidate or the designated hirer is vacant, skip that office: it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring: vacancies in ascending card-back number; consent from every other represented candidate-pool player; fatigue follows promotion.

answers.answer: The former Chairman first announces how many shares are needed for a pure majority (more than half the current shares). Any shareholder may campaign, and the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner's Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. If no candidate receives majority support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. The Chairman piece still counts as a Company share for dividends, majority, and scoring, but it cannot be traded or invested in a firm.
answers.evidence: Chairman election: pure majority, former Chairman resolves no-majority election; Chairman share counts but cannot be traded.

answers.answer: For a Company-office success check, first commit the required resources and cash; all check cash comes from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, roll, and use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails, with a retry allowed if resources and that office's limits permit; 5–6 is catastrophic. Catastrophe ends that office's actions, returns its officeholder to supply, discards its fatigue, and flips its card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander or firm procedures can modify this general procedure. Do not take an action that has no effect or chance of success, such as trading with no ship or deploying with no dice merely to trigger possible officer losses.
answers.evidence: Company Operation—Success checks: treasury payment, lowest die outcomes, retry and catastrophe destinations, and dead-action rule.

answers.answer: The Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, gaining £5 Balance per Debt. Each additional Debt advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman; the Chairman may never advance beyond the Debt track's end. The Chairman must then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by the amount transferred. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while observing the borrowing limits. Money already held in office treasuries remains there for those offices to use.
answers.evidence: Actions—Chairman: up to three free Debt, majority consent beyond, track limit, allocate all Balance.

answers.answer: The Manager of Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the shipyard owner's consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China if that office exists. Extra ships last only until Refresh.
answers.evidence: Actions—Manager of Shipping: spend to £2 or less; ship costs, consent and Company-ship prerequisite, destinations.

answers.answer: For Trade, declare the home region plus only regions reachable through open orders and within available ship capacity. Each £1 in the President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die for every declared nonhome region. A noncatastrophic failure may be retried during that President's uninterrupted opportunity if affordable; another position cannot act between attempts. Each Presidency may have at most one successful Trade per turn. On success, fill up to one order per ship in its sea zone, as many as possible within the declared regions. Put the first writer at the home port; every later order must be adjacent to one already filled by this Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President may not fill another President's home region, even if that other President's office is vacant. Company Balance rises by each order's full printed revenue, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn under deregulation. The President gets £1 from the bank per order, and each writer owner gets £1 per writer placed.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade: declaration/dice, order capacity and route, writers, home-region restriction, bonuses and limit.

answers.answer: A Commander may target their Presidency's home, any region associated with it, or a region bordering an associated region. They cannot target another Presidency's home or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company region is a legal target only if it has unrest or a closed order, so the action can have an effect. Exhaust each chosen officer or regiment for one die and each local alliance for its printed number of dice. Subtract the combined strength of the target and every other region in its empire, counting the target once; Company-controlled defense strength is zero. Roll the normal check and a noncatastrophic failure may be retried with remaining resources. After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll for officer losses.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: target restrictions, dice, empire-strength penalty, retries, and losses after each attempt.

answers.answer: On a successful Deploy, take loot from the bank equal to £4 per tower in the target plus its faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of one pound per surviving participating officer plus £1. Count only officers who survive this attempt, and the regiments and local-alliance pieces used in it. Distribute in repeated payout cycles: first £1 to the Commander plus £1 for each of the Commander's used surviving officers; then £1 per used surviving officer of each other family clockwise; then £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece to the bank. Stop paying when cash runs out, then repeat the cycle until all loot is distributed. The Commander gains one trophy per target tower. To impose control, remove the target's tower and dome, remove all matching empire flags if it was a capital, open all its orders and clear unrest; if the Elephant there pointed outward, put it fully inside the conquered region for Rebellion. On catastrophic failure, the Commander returns half their family's trophies, rounded up, and their member goes to supply. Exhausted officers still undergo the loss rolls; a Commander has no office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: loot minimum and payout cycle, trophy/control effects, and catastrophe outcome.

answers.answer: A Governor starts with the printed dice pool. For each attempt, roll the current pool without a penalty, then reduce the pool by one regardless of the result. On success, take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then choose exactly one benefit: Build, Commission a regiment, or Tax. Two successful Build choices are required: the first puts a partially built Company ship in the Governor's region if none is there, and the second completes it into the sea zone associated with that Governor's President. A commissioned regiment goes in that President's Army. Tax adds an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President's treasury; each Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in the region. Any unsuccessful attempt adds one regional unrest; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal check rule. Continue with the shrinking pool until choosing to stop, no dice remain, or catastrophe occurs.
answers.evidence: Governors: Administer: shrinking pool, success bonus/choice, destinations, repeated-Tax unrest and stopping.

answers.answer: During Revenue, first pay £1 per existing Debt, each officer and regiment in an Army, and each ship in a sea zone, including China; Commanders are excluded. If Balance cannot cover expenses, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one step per loan until the track ends. Keep taking emergency loans even at maximum Debt; newly added Debt creates no additional expense this turn. After using emergency loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with the expectations for current Standing and lower Standing one if Balance is below them. After that, the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, at one cash per Company share per dividend, paying each owner £1 per share including the Chairman. If total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one space.
answers.evidence: Revenue: expenses/emergency loans, Standing losses, expectations, then dividends and Standing gain.

answers.answer: When an Invasion or Rebellion attacks a Company region, it also triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary attack first, then secondary attacks in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order; in each Presidency its Commander orders the attacks. A normal primary Crisis uses the usual Invasion/Rebellion attack strength plus unrest in its target region. A primary Foreign Invasion instead uses only its ordinary attack die, with no unrest added. Each secondary Rebellion's attack strength is only the unrest cubes in that secondary region, with no modifier or empire strength. For each defense, the associated Commander exhausts active Army pieces whose total strength equals the attack strength, or as much as possible; local alliances use printed strength and cannot be split. If the newly exhausted defense is insufficient, apply Region Loss. If sufficient, remove all unrest in that region and give the Commander one trophy; if that successful defense defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one tower from the attacking region if possible. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts in their place, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; the acting player chooses defense pieces and neither gains nor loses trophies, and this does not appoint a Commander.
answers.evidence: Events—Attacks on Company and Region Loss: attack order/strength, defense sufficiency and successful-defense results.

answers.answer: A vote result of −1 or less fails: discard the law, resolve a dilemma's If Failed text if applicable, return the Opposition Leader token and give the PM dial to the Opposition Leader. The new PM moves the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. A result of zero or higher passes: place the law among passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy first, then the law's immediate effects. After either result, restore every card used for voting to its regular orientation. If a law causes Company failure, finish resolving the vote before Final Scoring. Thus support exactly zero passes. The proposal begins at the law's printed support; cash votes adjust support, and the policy selected before voting is the first dial space in the chosen direction matching the law's bottom icon.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Voting and Resolution: −1 fails, 0 passes, PM/policy changes and effect order.

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, before London Season at turn start, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. On passage, lower Debt by one for every two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. On failure, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping or placing the Court VP token, to a maximum of ±3. This special vote has no policy; failure neither removes the PM nor discards the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against it. 1813 starts deregulated. The summary describes this special vote's outcomes but does not give its ordinary vote-support resolution procedure.
answers.evidence: Deregulation: scenario timing/triggers and effects; summary says ‘No policy accompanies this law’ and records the special failure exceptions.

answers.answer: In the Firms phase after Family share creation and before Hiring, form a firm only if you currently manage none: return one eligible Company share to supply or flip a workshop to its invested side, flip your family board, place a family member as the first firm share, set the value cube at the leftmost track space, and take £5 from the bank into the London treasury. To invest in an existing firm, get the manager's consent and make the same Company-share or workshop contribution; it creates one firm share and puts £5 from the bank into London. A firm may have up to ten shares; further investments still add £5 but create no shares. The Chairman's share cannot be used, Company shares cannot be invested while Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and shares created that turn cannot be invested even if traded away. An invested workshop never returns to its uninvested side, gives no workshop bonus or Company-failure VP, and remains invested if its firm fails.
answers.evidence: Firms phase: investments: formation/investment cash, share cap and Company-share/workshop restrictions.

answers.answer: Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers simultaneously and secretly choose a trade zone/home port or Hobnob. A trade strategy requires at least one ship; its home port may be closed when selected, and it commits a secret bid from the London treasury. Reveal bids simultaneously, but keep strategy cards facedown until their matching Presidency begins. At that Presidency's start, before actions, matching firms reveal and roll one die per committed £1, paying the bid to the bank; at least one 1 or 2 permits trade. Firm initiative is ship count minus the number of successful bid dice (1s and 2s), possibly negative. A President that successfully trades gets initiative by the same formula using its ships. After the President's success, fill orders from lowest initiative first; the President chooses tie order. If the President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after Commander/Governor opportunities, and the Chairman resolves initiative ties. Each firm fills open orders from its chosen home port, tracing through its own filled route, up to ships plus one; it fills each particular order at most once. Firms may refill orders filled this turn by others or the Company, and the Company may refill firm orders. A previously filled order pays half its printed revenue, rounded down. Trade revenue goes to the firm's India treasury, and its Value advances one space per full £6 added to that treasury this turn. Hobnob makes no bid, trade, or dividends, but pays expenses and retains its prior dividend marker.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade: commitment, check timing, initiative, order filling, half revenue and Value growth.

answers.answer: At the start of Revenue, before the Company, firms pay expenses in initiative order, then the other firms; ties go to the manager with the most windows, then PM clockwise order. A firm owes £1 per charter ship plus the higher of its share count or firm Value. Pay using either or both firm treasuries. If unable to pay, it dissolves unless rescued: emergency investments follow normal Company-share/workshop rules, pay expenses, discard any remaining cash, and lower Value one space per emergency investment; alternatively, merge with one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if not already paid and then cover the endangered firm's shortfall. On dissolution, shares go to Debtor's Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to shipyards, the charter returns to the family side, and workshops stay invested. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends only from the India treasury. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager; with the manager's consent, a shareholder may forgo payment for any number of their shares on a dividend. Record the total cash actually paid out, not the per-share rate, as the dividend marker. An active non-Hobnob firm paying no dividend records zero; Hobnob keeps its previous marker. Sweep remaining India money into London after dividends. Firm cash is limited to specified procedures and is not family cash.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: cost/funding, rescue/dissolution destinations and dividend calculation.
